correctness.rationale: Replace both detections by complementary empty-box indicators, preserving covariance. Conditional on N=n, a specified box is empty with probability (1−t)^n and both are empty with probability (1−2t)^n. Hence C(t)=G(1−2t)−G(1−t)^2. Expanding G(1−t)=1−μt+vt²/2−wt³/6 gives the stated C(t)=t²F(t). For the entire allowed interval, F″≤−v(v−w)/2−2μw/3−w²t²/3, with v≥w≥0. If N can equal 2 or 3, this is strictly negative: for w=0 use v>0, and for w>0 use μ>0. Three distinct zeros would contradict strict concavity between the first and third. Two strictly interior zeros force negativity at both endpoints by the same strict chord inequality extended from either end and positivity between; those three signs conversely give two reversals. With N≤2 and b=P(N=1), c=P(N=2), F=2c−(b+2c−ct)² increases strictly when c>0; when c=0 it is constant −b², including the zero law. Independently expanding the two witness PGFs in integer coefficients gave 1024F=−57+680t−1558t²+504t³−81t⁴ and 100F=−44+120t−25t². Exact rational evaluation reproduced the five displayed three-copy signs (including zero at 1/9), and the two-copy root 2/5. No endpoint root is counted as a strict interior reversal. Read VERIFICATION.md and check.py as frozen evidence; the source program was not executed. The finite source tests do not substitute for the curvature bound.

value.rationale: Under the simple finite-disjoint-stock detection model, the theorem identifies precisely how many items are needed for a reentrant covariance sign pattern. It proves a distribution-uniform cap and supplies realizable interior witnesses, showing that a positive window alone need not indicate a common measurement fault. This is more than computing a PGF or restating conditioned negative association. It is a population probability result, not a validation of an assay, an estimator, or a field detection claim.
